skill.name: list-hygiene-monitor
skill.description: Monitors email-list decay, bounce and complaint trends, and suppression drift across scheduled reviews. Produces measured cohorts and re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists.
skill.summary: Monitor recurring email-list health and turn engagement decay into prioritized hygiene actions.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Fifty-six detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, repository-relative links, fixed memory paths, and homepage metadata. One medium-risk command pattern is confirmed: SKILL.md line 52 places the user-provided list identifier into shell examples without quoting. No evidence found of prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or an unauthorized external destination.

remediation.issue: The ledger command examples insert the list identifier as an unquoted shell argument.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the list identifier as a quoted argument, reject shell metacharacters, and use an argument-array execution API when the host supports one.

content.user_title: Monitor Email List Health and Decay
content.value_statement: Decaying engagement and suppression drift can harm sender reputation. This skill turns ESP exports and baselines into measured cohorts, trend alerts, and action worklists.
actual_capabilities: Groups subscribers into five engagement-recency cohorts using open or click timing.
Compares hard-bounce and spam-complaint rates with ESP benchmarks and prior baselines.
Checks suppression-list growth and identifies opt-out leakage against active recipients.
Produces measured or estimated re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists.
Assigns SEND S and E sub-item statuses without calculating the full EQS.
limitations: Requires ESP exports or connected own-account data; it cannot discover missing subscriber records.
Cannot calculate trend deltas without a prior baseline and marks them as NEEDS_INPUT.
Does not run authentication checks, own consent records, or calculate the full EQS.
Uses estimated starting thresholds that need tuning for each ESP and program.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Lifecycle Cleanup
use_cases.description: Segment dormant subscribers and create re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists before a win-back campaign.

use_cases.title: Investigate Reputation Drift
use_cases.description: Compare bounce and complaint rates with benchmarks and earlier runs, then identify conditions requiring a send hold.

use_cases.title: Audit Suppression Operations
use_cases.description: Reconcile active recipients with suppression history and surface opt-out leakage for correction.

prompt_templates.title: Review List Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my [program] list using this engagement and bounce export. Show recency cohorts, key risks, and an action worklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first hygiene review with one current export.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [current export] with [prior baseline] for [profile]. Calculate bounce, complaint, dormant, and suppression changes, then recommend the next watch.
prompt_templates.scenario: A recurring review with historical evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Suppression Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Cross-check [active list] against [suppression history]. Identify leakage, quantify affected records, classify SEND S and E, and propose safe remediation.
prompt_templates.scenario: An operations audit focused on honoring opt-outs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scheduled Hygiene Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [monthly or quarterly] hygiene process for [program]. Define cohort thresholds, evidence labels, escalation gates, saved baselines, and owner handoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced program design for repeated monitoring.

output_examples.input: Newsletter export with 20,000 subscribers and 4,000 inactive for more than 180 days.
output_examples.output: Deep-dormant: 4,000 of 20,000, Measured. Move clean records to re-permission, sunset nonresponders, and place bounced or complained records in prune.

output_examples.input: Current complaint rate is 0.12 percent, but no prior baseline is available.
output_examples.output: Complaint status: watch because it exceeds the 0.1 percent red line. Trend: NEEDS_INPUT until a prior report is supplied.

output_examples.input: The active list contains 18 addresses already recorded as unsubscribed.
output_examples.output: Suppression leakage: 18 Measured records. Hold the next send, remove these recipients, and route the N1 candidate evidence to the auditor.

best_practices: Use per-subscriber exports when possible and label derived cohort counts as Estimated.
Supply a prior baseline so the report can calculate real trend deltas.
Confirm the list profile, monitoring cadence, and save permission before producing persistent results.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret a falling open rate without checking bounce, complaint, and suppression evidence.
Do not re-permission addresses that hard-bounced, complained, or opted out.
Do not calculate the final EQS or overwrite the consent registry from this skill.

faq.question: Does this skill modify records in my ESP?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes supplied exports or connected reads and produces worklists. Apply changes through approved ESP and consent workflows.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide engagement recency, bounce and complaint reports, suppression history, list profile, cadence, and preferably a prior baseline.

faq.question: What happens when no baseline exists?
faq.answer: It reports current metrics and marks trend comparisons as NEEDS_INPUT. The current run can become the next baseline.

faq.question: How are subscribers grouped?
faq.answer: It uses active, cooling, dormant, deep-dormant, and never-engaged bands based on the most recent open or click.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically prune subscribers?
faq.answer: No. It creates a sized worklist and leaves record changes to the user and approved systems.

faq.question: Is this a complete deliverability audit?
faq.answer: No. It supplies list-hygiene evidence for another auditor; it does not test authentication or calculate final EQS.
